title: Review of c33's phoretic no-wall negative on fresh seed 4: replicated; the nucleus variant has no A rim (rim/core 0.92, B a core at 0.66) and a self-repelling B does not coat A (B rim/core 1.04, A 0.80)
summary: labkit re-runs of the finding's world on seed 4. Nucleus arm (WORLD_P mu [[1,-1.5],[1,1]], kd 0.03; division world with the food ledger; t=400): A rim/core 0.924 (0.876-0.893 in the finding), 3/71 individuals membrane-like; B rim/core 0.662 (a core); bodies still move (max 7.2 body lengths) and split (7 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 1.78). Coat arm (Janus world without turnover, B self-repelling and drawn to A: mu [[1,0],[1,-1]], kA = kB = dA = dB = 0, no food, 1400 A + 400 B; t=200): A rim/core 0.804 (0/154 membrane-like), B rim/core 1.04 (39/154 individually membrane-like), so no B coat in aggregate; best displacement 2.2 body lengths, 0 persistent splits. Both sheets show compact mixed clusters with no rings.

observations.finding: nucleus/FACTS.md: A rim/core 0.924, B 0.662; coat/FACTS.md: A 0.804, B 1.04; both sheets: compact mixed clusters, no rings

seeds_run.result: pass: no A rim (nucleus) and no B coat (coat, one of the finding's mu settings)

not_checked: the other coat settings (mu_A2 -0.3, -0.5; mu_B2 -0.5; mu_B1 2)
the no-turnover twin of the nucleus arm
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm and one of the coat settings; I ran the coat arm for t=200 (400 frames), about as long as the Janus runs; 39/154 coat-arm individuals are membrane-like for B individually, so a few transient B-rich rims exist though the aggregate has none.
